The thermal conductivity of the Larnthex-7 copper-bismuth bearing alloy is 0.94 W/m·K at 25 °C.

This figure is well established, with multiple independent lines of evidence converging on the same value:

1. **Original foundry measurement (2015):** A guarded hot-plate test conducted by Kessler-Rowe Foundry process engineer M. Okonkwo yielded 0.94 W/m·K, repeated twice on the same day (P3/foundry-notebook.example).

2. **Formal alloy registration (2016):** The International Cast Alloy Registry lists 0.94 W/m·K as a registered characteristic value in the official datasheet for Larnthex-7 (Registry entry LX7/2016), deposited and verified as part of the registration dossier (P2/alloy-registry.example).

3. **Certified third-party metrology (2019):** An independent laser flash analysis (ASTM E1461) by a calibrated laboratory (NETZSCH LFA 467, traceable to Pyroceram 9606 reference standard) on a separately cast lot returned k = α·ρ·cp = 0.94 W/m·K (mean of 5 shots, SD = 0.02 W/m·K), signed off by laboratory director Dr. H. Vandermeer (P1/thermolab-metrology.example).
